chapters.title: For Dad
chapters.text:
This book is for Martin Vale, who asked for it first.

He asked when I was seventeen, and again at twenty. I said yes both times and did nothing about it. This is late, and it is here.

chapters.title: Alder Vale
chapters.text:
The Vale family comes from Alder Vale, a settlement on the western bank of the Willow river. The parish there kept registers from the 1790s, and the name Vale appears in them from the beginning.

By the 1890s Alder Vale had a mill, a school and about sixty households. The 2010 count recorded ninety-one residents.

The surname and the place name are the same word. The settlement was named for the family, and the family carries the name of its ground.

chapters.title: Ellis Vale
chapters.text:
Ellis Vale was born about 1899 in Alder Vale. He worked as a harness-maker, and the trade is what the family remembers first.

He married Marta Vale, born about 1902. Their son Jonah was born about 1930.

Ellis died about 1971. Both of his years are approximate and come from family notes rather than a certificate.

chapters.text:
Jonah Vale was born about 1930 in Alder Vale and moved with his parents to Harbourfield as a boy.

He worked at the harbour for forty years. His son Martin was born in 1962.

Jonah died in 1998.

chapters.title: Martin Vale
chapters.text:
Martin Vale was born on 2 February 1962 in Willowford. He trained as a joiner and worked in Harbourfield.

With Clara Vale, born 1965 in Harbourfield, he brought up one son, Rowan.

Martin died on 9 June 2019.

chapters.title: The move to Harbourfield
chapters.text:
The move from Alder Vale to Harbourfield happened around 1946. Clara remembered the year from a story, not from a document, and it is printed as a story.

The photograph labelled as the family who left Alder Vale shows Ellis, Marta and Jonah. The old caption names Jonah on the left. It does not give a full order, so the rest is left open.

chapters.title: The harness-maker
chapters.text:
Of everything recorded about Ellis Vale, the part the family tells most often is the harness.

He worked with leather all his life. People came from the whole valley for his work. His funeral is remembered in the same terms.

chapters.text:
